posts.author: Patrick Moorhead
posts.role: Moor Insights & Strategy 창업자·수석 애널리스트(전 AMD CVP)
posts.text:
$AMD Q3: BEAT and raise, it's up sharply after hours: the market is paying for the $17B guide. Stellar execution; the pundits were wrong.

The numbers:
-Revenue $13.38B, +45% YoY, vs $13.08B consensus: BEAT
-Non-GAAP EPS $2.09 vs $1.93 consensus, $1.98 whisper: BEAT
-Non-GAAP gross margin 56% vs 56% guide: MEET
-Q4 guide ~$17.0B, +27% QoQ, vs $16.14B consensus: BEAT

Takeaways:
1. Friday I said that if AMD showed Intel's substrate pain, it's the market's problem. It didn't: AMD locked in wafers, substrates and memory early.

2. AMD expects data center up about 50% sequentially in Q4, so by my math the rest of AMD shrinks. With PCs soft and memory expensive, it's moving wafers to data center. AMD is a datacenter company.

3. Helios is running at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle. The cost: free cash flow fell to $554M on a $3.0B inventory build. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin: ~55%. 

Some analysts said Helios wouldn't even be ready by Q3. They were wrong.

@AMD $AMD

$AMD CEO Lisa Su:

“We now expect revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027,” more than twice the company's long-term growth target outlined last November.

Data Center is now expected to account for over 80% of AMD's total revenue in 2027, up from 64% in Q3.

Server CPU revenue is expected to double YoY in 2027, compared with the previous forecast of 70%+ growth.

Data Center AI revenue is expected to grow even faster than management projected just 90 days ago.

Su said customers have expanded their EPYC and Instinct deployment plans, while AMD has secured additional supply to support the higher growth outlook.

Looking beyond 2027, AMD is also working with multiple frontier AI labs to optimize its upcoming MI500 accelerators for their planned multi-gigawatt deployments.

posts.text:
$ANET +18%

JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY.

Arista beat Wall Street expectations in Q3 and guided Q4 above estimates, while introducing a 2027 outlook well ahead of expectations.

Despite ramping investments in AI networking, liquid cooling, and high-speed switching, Arista delivered a 49.1% adjusted operating margin.

The company also raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time this year to $13.3B, representing 48% annual growth.

Looking ahead to 2027, management expects approximately $18.5B in revenue, or 38%-40% growth. That's well above the roughly $16.4B analysts were modeling before earnings.

AI networking is expected to drive much of that growth.

Arista expects its AI fabrics business to approximately double from at least $3.5B in 2026 to around $7B in 2027, accounting for nearly 38% of total company revenue next year.

Meanwhile, its campus networking business is projected to grow 60% to approximately $2B.

CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista has now surpassed 100 Etherlink customers, compared with just four or five major AI customers when the company began its AI networking push a few years ago.

By the end of 2027, Arista expects more than 10 gigawatts of AI deployments across at least 10 different types of compute accelerators.

Another interesting development is the shift from centralized AI training toward distributed inference, where different parts of a workload, including prefill and token generation, run across separate systems.

That requires more networking capacity and more intelligent routing between GPUs, memory, and storage. Arista sees this as another growth opportunity beyond traditional AI data center networking.

The company is also expanding into scale-up Ethernet, which connects accelerators within and across racks, with customer trials expected in 2027 and production targeted for 2028.
